findings.reason: A module generated by images of a simple module is semisimple and isotypic of that type. A direct-sum coordinate projection is nonzero on every chosen nonzero vector for some coordinate. The monoid-algebra/intertwining-map equivalence transports this to representations. No finite-dimensionality or additional irreducible-constituent premise is needed. The original public extra premise is retained and unused. Final native check, exact type AST check, and empty-kernel dependency replay passed for the current source/helper hashes.

An intertwiner nonzero on a fixed vector sends it to a nonzero fixed vector. Thus compact-subgroup averaging is unnecessary once isotypic generation and irreducibility are used. Every nonzero submodule of a semisimple isotypic module contains a simple submodule equivalent to the type, giving the required embedding. The finite-family fixed-vector proof correctly restricts to the generated invariant submodule and invokes the same projection result. Existing hypotheses remain in public signatures.

The free codomain is projective, so Mathlib supplies a linear section. The section and kernel inclusion give a bijective linear map from codomain times kernel; its inverse supplies the kernel retraction. Finite projective modules over the existing local ring are free. This replaces explicit inverse-identity construction without changing assumptions.

Finite-rank equality provides an isomorphism of the subspaces, and Mathlib extends this to an automorphism of the finite-dimensional ambient space. The same extension applies to the basis isomorphism between the spans of independent tuples.

Surjective maps have injective dual maps. An isomorphism of their dual ranges extends to an automorphism of the ambient dual; transposing via finite-dimensional evaluation equivalences gives the desired automorphism intertwining the original surjections. Finiteness of the target is derived from the existing finite-dimensional source and surjectivity. The evaluation map of independent functionals is surjective because its dual is the injective basis-construction map. No finite-dimensionality of the original vector space is added to pi_surj.

All reviewed existing public declaration headers are byte-identical. Four representation files add only the Mathlib-only helper; the finite-family file adds IrreducibleProjectionExists, whose only project import is that helper. Linear-algebra imports are unchanged. These new edges cannot introduce a project import cycle.
